summary: Model artifact pulls hang during TLS validation when OCSP responder unreachable via customer's egress proxy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that model startups intermittently hang for ~45-60s during artifact download in their private deployment. Symptoms point to TLS validation delays rather than TCP connect or S3 5xx. Impact: model pull stalls cause cold-start latencies to spike, occasional task restarts when health-checks exceed 2m. Affects several live endpoints in prod-us-west and degrades user-facing latency for BrightPay features. Timeline: 2026-03-11 07:12 UTC - customer first reported slow model start; 2026-03-11 08:05 UTC - initial Support triage; 2026-03-12 02:13 UTC - SRE capture packet traces and run curl tests through customer's proxy. Expected behaviour: service should fetch model artifacts and proceed to startup within standard artifact fetch window (~3-5s for metadata, ~10-20s total for larger models). Actual behaviour: TLS handshake completes to artifact storage, then process blocks for ~30-60s before resuming; logs show repeated X509 verification delays and OpenSSL OCSP fetch timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private package v1.29 to customer's VPC with their egress-proxy configured
2) Trigger model route that is cold (no cached KV), observe serving runtime attempting to pull artifacts
3) Note model pull logs and wall-clock time for startup
4) Repeat with direct internet egress (bypass proxy) - behavior does not reproduce
logs: [2026-03-11T07:31:05Z] serving-runtime: opening TLS connection to storage.redwood-models.com:443
[2026-03-11T07:31:06Z] serving-runtime: TLS handshake complete; starting certificate verification
[2026-03-11T07:31:37Z] serving-runtime: certificate verification blocked on OCSP fetch (timeout after 30s)
[2026-03-11T07:31:38Z] serving-runtime: falling back to CRL check; continuing with artifact download
[2026-03-11T07:33:12Z] health-check: model-pod restart due to probe timeout
investigation_notes: Captured tcpdump on node: observed repeated SYN->SYN/ACK to storage endpoint but no connection attempts to known OCSP responders while egressing via corporate proxy.

Replayed curl through customer's proxy: 'curl -v https://storage.redwood-models.com' stalls during OCSP HTTP GET to ocsp.example-ca.com and finally succeeds after proxy returns 504 then forwards to internet (total ~35s).

Proxy behaviour: BrightPay's egress proxy performs TLS termination and re-signing, but is not configured to cache/staple OCSP responses. Proxy blocks outbound TCP to port 80/443 for ocsp.example-ca.com; it attempts a synchronous fetch and waits for upstream which times out only after long retry windows.

OpenSSL behavior: runtime attempts real-time OCSP query to a CA responder; when proxy delays this fetch the verification call blocks the certificate validation path and stalls the handshake verification process for ~30s before falling back.

Hypothesis: egress proxy's blocking/queueing of OCSP responder traffic causes certificate verification to block under default OpenSSL timeout, leading to long artifact pull delays. Bypass/proxyless egress shows normal behaviour.
Confirmed by adding an allow rule for ocsp.example-ca.com in customer's proxy ACLs -> model pulls returned to normal startup times in subsequent test deploys.
comments: Support (Aisha): Initial triage - asked for environment details, pod logs, and whether workaround (bypass proxy) was possible.
Customer (BrightPay IT - Daniel): Confirmed they enforce strict egress ACLs and proxy-based TLS inspection; provided proxy logs showing OCSP requests queued.
SRE (Marco): Collected tcpdump and ran curl with --verbose through proxy; reproduced the OCSP stall; suggested temporary allowlist for OCSP responders and enabling OCSP stapling on proxy.
Customer: Applied allowlist for ocsp.example-ca.com and retested. Verified cold-start improved from 45-60s down to 6-12s. Asked for recommended permanent mitigation.
Support: Recommended steps documented and coordinated with Customer Success to schedule permanent change and follow-up.
resolution: Workaround: Customer added explicit egress allow-rule for primary OCSP responder domains (ocsp.example-ca.com, ocsp2.example-ca.com) and enabled OCSP stapling/caching on their egress proxy; immediate improvement observed. Root cause: corporate egress proxy queued/blocked OCSP fetches causing OpenSSL certificate verification to block the artifact pull path. Permanent action items: 1) Customer to maintain allowlist for CA OCSP endpoints or enable stapling for upstream TLS; 2) Redwood to add documentation for private deployments describing OCSP/CRL requirements and recommended proxy configs; 3) Runtime change: introduce configurable OCSP_FETCH_TIMEOUT (default 3s) and a graceful verification fallback in runtime v1.32.0 (PR linked). Follow-up: coordinate with Customer Success for verification after firewall rule rollout and update KB article.
